1→# Implement API rate limiting to prevent abuse
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Most API routes lack rate limiting protection. While the /api/service-request endpoint has a 30-second cooldown per table, other sensitive endpoints like /api/locations (POST), /api/menu/publish (POST), /api/qr/generate (POST), and authentication endpoints have no rate limiting.
     6→
     7→## Rationale
     8→
     9→Without rate limiting, attackers can perform brute-force attacks on authentication, exhaust resources through API abuse, or spam the system with automated requests. This is especially critical for a SaaS platform where resource abuse affects all tenants.
    10→
    11→---
    12→*This spec was created from ideation and is pending detailed specification.*
    13→

1→# ozaMenu - Dijital QR Menu ve Fiyat Defteri Platformu
     2→
     3→[![Next.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/Next.js-15.5-black?logo=next.js)](https://nextjs.org/)
     4→[![TypeScript](https://img.shields.io/badge/TypeScript-5.7-blue?logo=typescript)](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
     5→[![Supabase](https://img.shields.io/badge/Supabase-PostgreSQL-green?logo=supabase)](https://supabase.com/)
     6→[![Tailwind CSS](https://img.shields.io/badge/Tailwind-4.x-38B2AC?logo=tailwind-css)](https://tailwindcss.com/)
     7→
     8→**Turkiye'deki restoran, kafe ve benzeri isletmeler icin Ticaret Bakanligi regulasyonlarina uyumlu Dijital Fiyat Defteri ve QR Menu SaaS platformu.**
     9→
    10→## Icindekiler
    11→
    12→- [Proje Hakkinda](#proje-hakkinda)
    13→- [Ozellikler](#ozellikler)
    14→- [Teknoloji Yigini](#teknoloji-yigini)
    15→- [On Kosullar](#on-kosullar)
    16→- [Kurulum](#kurulum)
    17→- [Ortam Degiskenleri](#ortam-degiskenleri)
    18→- [Veritabani Kurulumu](#veritabani-kurulumu)
    19→- [Gelistirme](#gelistirme)
    20→- [Test](#test)
    21→- [Proje Yapisi](#proje-yapisi)
    22→- [Paket Ozellikleri](#paket-ozellikleri)
    23→- [Deployment](#deployment)
    24→- [Mimari Kararlar](#mimari-kararlar)
    25→- [Katki](#katki)
    26→- [Lisans](#lisans)
    27→
    28→---
    29→
    30→## Proje Hakkinda
    31→
    32→ozaMenu, isletmelerin dijital menuleri yonetmelerini saglayan, hukuki uyumlu bir SaaS platformudur. Platform, sadece gorsel bir menu degil, **yasal olarak gecerli, denetlenebilir ve degismez fiyat kaydi tutan** bir sistemdir.
    33→
    34→### Temel Avantajlar
    35→
    36→- **Hukuki Uyumluluk**: Ticaret Bakanligi regulasyonlarina uygun fiyat defteri
    37→- **Degismez Kayit**: Fiyat degisiklikleri INSERT-only pattern ile saklanir, UPDATE/DELETE yasak
    38→- **Multi-Tenant Mimari**: Her isletme sadece kendi verisine erisebilir (RLS ile korunur)
    39→- **Masa Bazli QR**: Musterinin hangi masada oturdugu bilinir, garson bildirimleri
    40→- **Dinamik Paket Yonetimi**: Hard-coded limit yok, tum ozellikler veritabanindan yonetilir
    41→
    42→---
    43→
    44→## Ozellikler
    45→
    46→### Temel Ozellikler
    47→
    48→| Ozellik | Aciklama |
    49→|---------|----------|
    50→| Degismez Fiyat Defteri | Tum fiyat degisiklikleri tarihce olarak saklanir, hukuki kanit niteliginde |
    51→| Multi-Tenant Izolasyon | RLS politikalari ile isletmeler arasi veri izolasyonu |
    52→| Dinamik Feature Flags | Paket ozellikleri veritabanindan yonetilir, kod degisikligi gerektirmez |
    53→| Masa QR Sistemi | Her masaya ozel QR kod, musteri takibi |
    54→| Realtime Garson Bildirimleri | Supabase Realtime ile anlik bildirimler |
    55→| SHA-256 Menu Snapshot | Her fiyat degisikliginde menu durumu hash'lenir |
    56→| RBAC Yetkilendirme | Owner, Admin, Manager, Waiter, Viewer rolleri |
    57→
    58→### Panel Ozellikleri
    59→
    60→- **Merchant Paneli**: Urun, kategori, masa yonetimi, fiyat guncelleme
    61→- **Super Admin Paneli**: Isletme aktivasyonu, paket yonetimi, ozel izinler
    62→- **Garson Paneli**: Realtime servis talepleri, masa durumu
    63→- **Audit Log**: Tum islemlerin denetim kaydi
    64→
    65→---
    66→
    67→## Teknoloji Yigini
    68→
    69→### Frontend
    70→| Teknoloji | Versiyon | Aciklama |
    71→|-----------|----------|----------|
    72→| Next.js | 15.5.x | React framework (App Router) |
    73→| TypeScript | 5.7.x | Tip guvenli JavaScript |
    74→| Tailwind CSS | 4.x | Utility-first CSS framework |
    75→| React | 19.x | UI kutuphanesi |
    76→
    77→### Backend & Veritabani
    78→| Teknoloji | Aciklama |
    79→|-----------|----------|
    80→| Supabase | PostgreSQL, Auth, Realtime, Storage |
    81→| PostgreSQL | Iliskisel veritabani |
    82→| Row Level Security | Veri izolasyonu |
    83→
    84→### Araclar
    85→| Arac | Aciklama |
    86→|------|----------|
    87→| Vitest | Test framework |
    88→| ESLint | Kod kalitesi |
    89→| QRCode | QR kod uretimi |
    90→
    91→---
    92→
    93→## On Kosullar
    94→
    95→Projeyi calistirmadan once asagidakilerin kurulu olmasi gerekmektedir:
    96→
    97→1. **Node.js** >= 20.9
    98→   ```bash
    99→   # Node.js versiyonunu kontrol edin
   100→   node --version
   101→
   102→   # nvm kullaniyorsaniz
   103→   nvm install 20
   104→   nvm use 20
   105→   ```
   106→
   107→2. **npm** veya **pnpm**
   108→   ```bash
   109→   npm --version
   110→   ```
   111→
   112→3. **Supabase Hesabi**
   113→   - [supabase.com](https://supabase.com) adresinden ucretsiz hesap olusturun
   114→   - Yeni bir proje olusturun
   115→
   116→4. **Git**
   117→   ```bash
   118→   git --version
   119→   ```
   120→
   121→---
   122→
   123→## Kurulum
   124→
   125→### 1. Repoyu Klonlama
   126→
   127→```bash
   128→git clone https://github.com/your-org/ozon-qr-menu.git
   129→cd ozon-qr-menu
   130→```
   131→
   132→### 2. Bagimliliklari Yukleme
   133→
   134→```bash
   135→npm install
   136→```
   137→
   138→### 3. Ortam Degiskenlerini Ayarlama
   139→
   140→```bash
   141→# Ornek dosyayi kopyalayin
   142→cp .env.local.example .env.local
   143→
   144→# Dosyayi duzenleyin ve Supabase bilgilerinizi girin
   145→nano .env.local  # veya tercih ettiginiz editoru kullanin
   146→```
   147→
   148→### 4. Veritabani Migrasyonlarini Calistirma
   149→
   150→Supabase Dashboard uzerinden veya Supabase CLI ile migrasyonlari calistirin:
   151→
   152→```bash
   153→# Supabase CLI kurulumu (opsiyonel)
   154→npm install -g supabase
   155→
   156→# Local Supabase baslat (opsiyonel - gelistirme icin)
   157→npx supabase start
   158→
   159→# Migrasyonlari uygula
   160→npx supabase db push
   161→```
   162→
   163→Manuel olarak Supabase Dashboard > SQL Editor uzerinden de calistirabilirsiniz:
   164→1. `supabase/migrations/` klasorundeki dosyalari sirayla calistirin
   165→2. `supabase/seed.sql` dosyasini calistirarak baslangic verisini ekleyin
   166→
   167→### 5. Gelistirme Sunucusunu Baslatma
   168→
   169→```bash
   170→npm run dev
   171→```
   172→
   173→Uygulama [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) adresinde calisacaktir.
   174→
   175→---
   176→
   177→## Ortam Degiskenleri
   178→
   179→`.env.local` dosyasinda asagidaki degiskenleri tanimlayin:
   180→
   181→```env
   182→# Supabase Project URL
   183→# Supabase Dashboard > Settings > API > Project URL
   184→NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=https://your-project-ref.supabase.co
   185→
   186→# Supabase Anonymous (Public) Key
   187→# Supabase Dashboard > Settings > API > Project API keys > anon public
   188→# Bu anahtar client-side'da guvenle kullanilabilir (RLS ile korunur)
   189→NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=your-anon-key-here
   190→
   191→# Supabase Service Role Key (GIZLI - ASLA CLIENT'A EXPOSE ETME!)
   192→# Supabase Dashboard > Settings > API > Project API keys > service_role
   193→# Bu anahtar RLS'i bypass eder, sadece server-side'da kullanin
   194→SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=your-service-role-key-here
   195→```
   196→
   197→### Ortam Degiskenlerini Bulma
   198→
   199→1. [Supabase Dashboard](https://supabase.com/dashboard) adresine gidin
   200→2. Projenizi secin
   201→3. **Settings** > **API** bolumune gidin
   202→4. Asagidaki degerleri kopyalayin:
   203→   - **Project URL** → `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`
   204→   - **anon public** → `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`
   205→   - **service_role** → `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`
   206→
   207→> **UYARI**: `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` anahtarini asla client-side kodunda kullanmayin veya Git'e commit etmeyin!
   208→
   209→---
   210→
   211→## Veritabani Kurulumu
   212→
   213→### Migrasyon Dosyalari
   214→
   215→Veritabani semasi asagidaki migrasyon dosyalariyla olusturulur:
   216→
   217→| Dosya | Aciklama |
   218→|-------|----------|
   219→| `001_core_tables.sql` | Organizations, members, categories tablolari |
   220→| `002_products_price_ledger.sql` | Products ve immutable price_ledger |
   221→| `003_package_management.sql` | Features, plans, subscriptions |
   222→| `004_tables_service_requests.sql` | Masa ve garson sistemi |
   223→| `005_audit_compliance.sql` | Menu snapshots ve audit logs |
   224→| `006_views.sql` | current_prices ve diger view'lar |
   225→| `007_rls_policies.sql` | Row Level Security politikalari |
   226→| `010_auto_snapshot_trigger.sql` | Otomatik snapshot trigger'i |
   227→
   228→### Seed Data
   229→
   230→`supabase/seed.sql` dosyasi asagidaki baslangic verisini icerir:
   231→
   232→- **Features Katalogu**: 27 farkli ozellik tanimlamasi
   233→- **Paket Tanimlari**: Lite, Pro, Premium paketleri
   234→- **Paket-Ozellik Eslesmeleri**: Her paketin hangi ozelliklere sahip oldugu
   235→
   236→### Migrasyonlari Elle Calistirma
   237→
   238→Supabase Dashboard > SQL Editor'de sirayla:
   239→
   240→```sql
   241→-- Her dosyayi sirayla kopyalayip calistirin
   242→-- 1. supabase/migrations/001_core_tables.sql
   243→-- 2. supabase/migrations/002_products_price_ledger.sql
   244→-- ... devam edin
   245→-- Son olarak seed.sql dosyasini calistirin
   246→```
   247→
   248→---
   249→

1→import { createServerClient } from '@supabase/ssr'
     2→import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
     3→import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
     4→
     5→/**
     6→ * Service Request API Route Handler
     7→ *
     8→ * Creates waiter call / service requests from customers.
     9→ * This is a public endpoint - no authentication required since customers
    10→ * scan QR codes without logging in.
    11→ *
    12→ * POST /api/service-request
    13→ *
    14→ * Request body:
    15→ * {
    16→ *   tableId: string (required) - Table's qr_uuid from the QR code URL
    17→ *   requestType?: 'waiter_call' | 'bill_request' | 'other' (optional, default: 'waiter_call')
    18→ *   notes?: string (optional) - Additional message from customer
    19→ * }
    20→ *
    21→ * Response:
    22→ * {
    23→ *   success: boolean
    24→ *   data?: {
    25→ *     requestId: string - Created service request ID
    26→ *     tableNumber: string - Human-readable table number
    27→ *   }
    28→ *   error?: string
    29→ * }
    30→ *
    31→ * Features:
    32→ * - Spam prevention: 30-second cooldown between requests per table
    33→ * - Table status update: Sets table to 'service_needed'
    34→ * - Triggers Supabase Realtime notification for waiters
    35→ */
    36→
    37→/**
    38→ * Request type enum matching database CHECK constraint
    39→ */
    40→type ServiceRequestType = 'waiter_call' | 'bill_request' | 'other'
    41→
    42→/**
    43→ * Request body interface
    44→ */
    45→interface ServiceRequestBody {
    46→  tableId?: string
    47→  requestType?: ServiceRequestType
    48→  notes?: string
    49→}
    50→
    51→/**
    52→ * Spam prevention interval in milliseconds (30 seconds)
    53→ */
    54→const SPAM_PREVENTION_INTERVAL_MS = 30 * 1000
    55→
    56→/**
    57→ * Create Supabase server client with cookie handling
    58→ */
    59→async function createSupabaseClient() {
    60→  const cookieStore = await cookies()
    61→  return createServerClient(
    62→    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL!,
    63→    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!,
    64→    {
    65→      cookies: {
    66→        getAll() {
    67→          return cookieStore.getAll()
    68→        },
    69→        setAll(cookiesToSet) {
    70→          try {
    71→            cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =>
    72→              cookieStore.set(name, value, options)
    73→            )
    74→          } catch {
    75→            // The `setAll` method was called from a Server Component.
    76→            // This can be ignored if you have middleware refreshing user sessions.
    77→          }
    78→        },
    79→      },
    80→    }
    81→  )
    82→}
    83→
    84→/**
    85→ * Validate UUID format
    86→ */
    87→function isValidUUID(value: string): boolean {
    88→  const uuidRegex =
    89→    /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[1-5][0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i
    90→  return uuidRegex.test(value)
    91→}
    92→
    93→/**
    94→ * POST /api/service-request
    95→ *
    96→ * Creates a service request (waiter call) for a table.
    97→ * Public endpoint - no authentication required.
    98→ */
    99→export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {
   100→  const supabase = await createSupabaseClient()
   101→
   102→  // Parse request body
   103→  let body: ServiceRequestBody
   104→
   105→  try {
   106→    body = await request.json()
   107→  } catch {
   108→    return NextResponse.json(
   109→      { success: false, error: 'Gecersiz istek formati' },
   110→      { status: 400 }
   111→    )
   112→  }
   113→
   114→  // Validate required tableId field
   115→  if (!body.tableId || typeof body.tableId !== 'string') {
   116→    return NextResponse.json(
   117→      { success: false, error: 'Masa bilgisi (tableId) zorunludur' },
   118→      { status: 400 }
   119→    )
   120→  }
   121→
   122→  const tableId = body.tableId.trim()
   123→
   124→  // Validate UUID format
   125→  if (!isValidUUID(tableId)) {
   126→    return NextResponse.json(
   127→      { success: false, error: 'Gecersiz masa kimlik formati' },
   128→      { status: 400 }
   129→    )
   130→  }
   131→
   132→  // Validate request type
   133→  const validRequestTypes: ServiceRequestType[] = [
   134→    'waiter_call',
   135→    'bill_request',
   136→    'other',
   137→  ]
   138→  const requestType: ServiceRequestType =
   139→    body.requestType && validRequestTypes.includes(body.requestType)
   140→      ? body.requestType
   141→      : 'waiter_call'
   142→
   143→  // Validate notes length (prevent abuse)
   144→  const notes = body.notes?.trim().slice(0, 500) || null
   145→
   146→  // Fetch table by qr_uuid
   147→  const { data: table, error: tableError } = await supabase
   148→    .from('restaurant_tables')
   149→    .select('id, organization_id, table_number, last_ping_at, is_active')
   150→    .eq('qr_uuid', tableId)
   151→    .single()
   152→
   153→  if (tableError || !table) {
   154→    return NextResponse.json(
   155→      { success: false, error: 'Masa bulunamadi' },
   156→      { status: 404 }
   157→    )
   158→  }
   159→
   160→  // Check if table is active
   161→  if (!table.is_active) {
   162→    return NextResponse.json(
   163→      { success: false, error: 'Bu masa aktif degil' },
   164→      { status: 400 }
   165→    )
   166→  }
   167→
   168→  // Spam prevention: Check last_ping_at
   169→  if (table.last_ping_at) {
   170→    const lastPing = new Date(table.last_ping_at).getTime()
   171→    const now = Date.now()
   172→
   173→    if (now - lastPing < SPAM_PREVENTION_INTERVAL_MS) {
   174→      const remainingSeconds = Math.ceil(
   175→        (SPAM_PREVENTION_INTERVAL_MS - (now - lastPing)) / 1000
   176→      )
   177→      return NextResponse.json(
   178→        {
   179→          success: false,
   180→          error: `Lutfen ${remainingSeconds} saniye bekleyin`,
   181→        },
   182→        { status: 429 } // Too Many Requests
   183→      )
   184→    }
   185→  }
   186→
   187→  // Create service request
   188→  const { data: serviceRequest, error: insertError } = await supabase
   189→    .from('service_requests')
   190→    .insert({
   191→      organization_id: table.organization_id,
   192→      table_id: table.id,
   193→      request_type: requestType,
   194→      status: 'pending',
   195→      notes: notes,
   196→    })
   197→    .select('id')
   198→    .single()
   199→
   200→  if (insertError) {
   201→    return NextResponse.json(
   202→      {
   203→        success: false,
   204→        error: 'Servis istegi olusturulamadi. Lutfen tekrar deneyin.',
   205→      },
   206→      { status: 500 }
   207→    )
   208→  }
   209→
   210→  // Update table status and last_ping_at for spam prevention
   211→  const { error: updateError } = await supabase
   212→    .from('restaurant_tables')
   213→    .update({
   214→      current_status: 'service_needed',
   215→      last_ping_at: new Date().toISOString(),
   216→    })
   217→    .eq('id', table.id)
   218→
   219→  if (updateError) {
   220→    // Log but don't fail - the service request was created successfully
   221→    // The table status update is a secondary operation
   222→  }
   223→
   224→  return NextResponse.json({
   225→    success: true,
   226→    data: {
   227→      requestId: serviceRequest.id,
   228→      tableNumber: table.table_number,
   229→    },
   230→  })
   231→}
   232→

1→/**
     2→ * Rate Limiter Service - Dual Storage Strategy
     3→ *
     4→ * This service implements rate limiting for API endpoints using two strategies:
     5→ * 1. Database-backed (Supabase) for authenticated users - persistent across instances
     6→ * 2. In-memory (Map) for IP-based limits - fast, temporary tracking
     7→ *
     8→ * Features:
     9→ * - Configurable request limits and time windows
    10→ * - Automatic cleanup of expired entries (in-memory)
    11→ * - Turkish error messages for consistency
    12→ * - Result types for type-safe error handling
    13→ *
    14→ * Usage:
    15→ * - For authenticated endpoints: Use user ID as identifier with database strategy
    16→ * - For public endpoints: Use IP address as identifier with memory strategy
    17→ *
    18→ * @example
    19→ * // Check rate limit for authenticated user
    20→ * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('user-123', 20, 60000, 'database')
    21→ * if (!result.allowed) {
    22→ *   return NextResponse.json({ error: result.error }, { status: 429 })
    23→ * }
    24→ *
    25→ * // Check rate limit for IP address
    26→ * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('192.168.1.1', 10, 60000, 'memory')
    27→ */
    28→
    29→import { createServerSupabaseClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'
    30→
    31→/**
    32→ * Storage strategy for rate limiting
    33→ * - database: Persistent storage in Supabase for authenticated users
    34→ * - memory: In-memory Map for IP-based limits (faster, temporary)
    35→ */
    36→export type RateLimitStrategy = 'database' | 'memory'
    37→
    38→/**
    39→ * Result of rate limit check
    40→ */
    41→export interface RateLimitResult {
    42→  /** Whether the request is allowed */
    43→  allowed: boolean
    44→  /** Current request count in the window */
    45→  currentCount: number
    46→  /** Maximum allowed requests */
    47→  limit: number
    48→  /** Time remaining in milliseconds until reset */
    49→  resetIn: number
    50→  /** Error message if not allowed (in Turkish) */
    51→  error?: string
    52→  /** Timestamp when the rate limit window resets */
    53→  resetAt: Date
    54→}
    55→
    56→/**
    57→ * Result of reset operation
    58→ */
    59→export interface ResetLimitResult {
    60→  /** Whether the operation succeeded */
    61→  success: boolean
    62→  /** Error message if operation failed */
    63→  error?: string
    64→}
    65→
    66→/**
    67→ * In-memory rate limit entry
    68→ */
    69→interface RateLimitEntry {
    70→  /** Number of requests made in current window */
    71→  count: number
    72→  /** Timestamp when the window started */
    73→  windowStart: number
    74→  /** Window duration in milliseconds */
    75→  windowDuration: number
    76→}
    77→
    78→/**
    79→ * Rate Limiter Service
    80→ *
    81→ * Provides rate limiting functionality with dual storage strategy.
    82→ * Automatically cleans up expired entries from in-memory storage.
    83→ */
    84→export class RateLimiterService {
    85→  /** In-memory storage for IP-based rate limits */
    86→  private memoryStore: Map<string, RateLimitEntry> = new Map()
    87→
    88→  /** Cleanup interval ID for automatic expired entry removal */
    89→  private cleanupIntervalId?: NodeJS.Timeout
    90→
    91→  /** Cleanup interval in milliseconds (default: 5 minutes) */
    92→  private readonly CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000
    93→
    94→  constructor() {
    95→    // Start automatic cleanup of expired entries
    96→    this.startCleanup()
    97→  }
    98→
    99→  /**
   100→   * Check if request is allowed within rate limit
   101→   *
   102→   * @param identifier - User ID (for database) or IP address (for memory)
   103→   * @param limit - Maximum number of requests allowed in window
   104→   * @param windowMs - Time window in milliseconds
   105→   * @param strategy - Storage strategy to use ('database' or 'memory')
   106→   * @returns Promise<RateLimitResult> - Rate limit check result
   107→   *
   108→   * @example
   109→   * ```typescript
   110→   * // Check user rate limit (20 requests per minute)
   111→   * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('user-123', 20, 60000, 'database')
   112→   *
   113→   * // Check IP rate limit (10 requests per minute)
   114→   * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('192.168.1.1', 10, 60000, 'memory')
   115→   * ```
   116→   */
   117→  async checkRateLimit(
   118→    identifier: string,
   119→    limit: number,
   120→    windowMs: number,
   121→    strategy: RateLimitStrategy = 'memory'
   122→  ): Promise<RateLimitResult> {
   123→    if (strategy === 'database') {
   124→      return this.checkDatabaseRateLimit(identifier, limit, windowMs)
   125→    } else {
   126→      return this.checkMemoryRateLimit(identifier, limit, windowMs)
   127→    }
   128→  }
   129→
   130→  /**
   131→   * Reset rate limit for an identifier
   132→   *
   133→   * @param identifier - User ID or IP address to reset
   134→   * @param strategy - Storage strategy to use ('database' or 'memory')
   135→   * @returns Promise<ResetLimitResult> - Reset operation result
   136→   *
   137→   * @example
   138→   * ```typescript
   139→   * await rateLimiter.resetLimit('user-123', 'database')
   140→   * ```
   141→   */
   142→  async resetLimit(
   143→    identifier: string,
   144→    strategy: RateLimitStrategy = 'memory'
   145→  ): Promise<ResetLimitResult> {
   146→    try {
   147→      if (strategy === 'database') {
   148→        const supabase = await createServerSupabaseClient()
   149→
   150→        const { error } = await supabase
   151→          .from('rate_limits')
   152→          .delete()
   153→          .eq('identifier', identifier)
   154→
   155→        if (error) {
   156→          return {
   157→            success: false,
   158→            error: 'Rate limit sifirlama basarisiz',
   159→          }
   160→        }
   161→
   162→        return { success: true }
   163→      } else {
   164→        // Memory strategy
   165→        this.memoryStore.delete(identifier)
   166→        return { success: true }
   167→      }
   168→    } catch (error) {
   169→      return {
   170→        success: false,
   171→        error: 'Rate limit sifirlama sirasinda hata olustu',
   172→      }
   173→    }
   174→  }
   175→
   176→  /**
   177→   * Check rate limit using database storage (Supabase)
   178→   *
   179→   * @private
   180→   */
   181→  private async checkDatabaseRateLimit(
   182→    identifier: string,
   183→    limit: number,
   184→    windowMs: number
   185→  ): Promise<RateLimitResult> {
   186→    try {
   187→      const supabase = await createServerSupabaseClient()
   188→      const now = Date.now()
   189→      const windowStart = now - windowMs
   190→
   191→      // Fetch or create rate limit entry
   192→      const { data: existing, error: fetchError } = await supabase
   193→        .from('rate_limits')
   194→        .select('*')
   195→        .eq('identifier', identifier)
   196→        .single()
   197→
   198→      if (fetchError && fetchError.code !== 'PGRST116') {
   199→        // PGRST116 = not found, which is ok
   200→        // Log other errors but allow the request
   201→        return this.createAllowedResult(1, limit, windowMs, now)
   202→      }
   203→
   204→      if (!existing) {
   205→        // First request - create new entry
   206→        const { error: insertError } = await supabase
   207→          .from('rate_limits')
   208→          .insert({
   209→            identifier,
   210→            count: 1,
   211→            window_start: new Date(now).toISOString(),
   212→            window_duration_ms: windowMs,
   213→          })
   214→
   215→        if (insertError) {
   216→          // If insert fails, allow the request (fail open)
   217→          return this.createAllowedResult(1, limit, windowMs, now)
   218→        }
   219→
   220→        return this.createAllowedResult(1, limit, windowMs, now)
   221→      }
   222→
   223→      const entryWindowStart = new Date(existing.window_start).getTime()
   224→

   226→      if (now - entryWindowStart > windowMs) {

## ✅ Subtask 1-2 Completed Successfully

I've successfully created the rate limit middleware helper at `lib/middleware/rate-limit.ts`. Here's what was implemented:

### Key Features:

1. **`withRateLimit()` Higher-Order Function**
   - Wraps API route handlers with rate limiting logic
   - Type-safe with TypeScript generics
   - Follows Next.js App Router API route patterns

2. **Flexible Identifier Extraction**
   - **User ID-based**: Extracts authenticated user from Supabase session (uses database strategy)
   - **IP-based**: Extracts client IP from headers (x-real-ip, x-forwarded-for, or request.ip) (uses memory strategy)
   - **Custom**: Supports custom identifier extraction via callback function

3. **Comprehensive Rate Limit Response**
   - Returns HTTP 429 status when limit exceeded
   - Turkish error messages for consistency
   - Standard rate limit headers:
     - `X-RateLimit-Limit`: Maximum requests allowed
     - `X-RateLimit-Remaining`: Requests remaining in window
     - `X-RateLimit-Reset`: When the limit resets
     - `Retry-After`: Seconds to wait before retry

4. **Pre-configured Presets**
   - `cpuIntensive`: 20 req/min per user (for QR generation)

   - `databaseIntensive`: 10 req/min per user (for menu publish)
   - `publicEndpoint`: 10 req/min per IP (for logout)
   - `standard`: 30 req/min per user (general endpoints)

5. **Fail-Open Design**
   - If any error occurs during rate limit check, request is allowed
   - Ensures service availability over strict enforcement

1→# Implement API rate limiting to prevent abuse
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Most API routes lack rate limiting protection. While the /api/service-request endpoint has a 30-second cooldown per table, other sensitive endpoints like /api/locations (POST), /api/menu/publish (POST), /api/qr/generate (POST), and authentication endpoints have no rate limiting.
     6→
     7→## Rationale
     8→
     9→Without rate limiting, attackers can perform brute-force attacks on authentication, exhaust resources through API abuse, or spam the system with automated requests. This is especially critical for a SaaS platform where resource abuse affects all tenants.
    10→

    84→const RATE_LIMIT_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * 1000

    87→ * Request body interface

1→# Implement API rate limiting to prevent abuse
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Most API routes lack rate limiting protection. While the /api/service-request endpoint has a 30-second cooldown per table, other sensitive endpoints like /api/locations (POST), /api/menu/publish (POST), /api/qr/generate (POST), and authentication endpoints have no rate limiting.
     6→
     7→## Rationale
     8→
     9→Without rate limiting, attackers can perform brute-force attacks on authentication, exhaust resources through API abuse, or spam the system with automated requests. This is especially critical for a SaaS platform where resource abuse affects all tenants.

1→# e-menum.net Route Documentation
     2→
     3→This document provides a comprehensive overview of all routes in the e-menum.net platform, including pages, API endpoints, and their access requirements.

    22→
    23→The e-menum.net platform uses Next.js App Router with route groups for organization:
    24→

    26→|-------------|---------|---------------|
    27→| `(public)` | Public pages (landing, features, pricing) | No |
    28→| `(auth)` | Authentication pages (login, register) | No |
    29→| `(dashboard)` | Merchant dashboard pages | Yes |
    30→| `(admin)` | Super Admin panel | Yes (Super Admin) |
    31→| `/menu/[slug]` | Public menu pages (QR target) | No |
    32→| `/api/*` | API endpoints | Varies |
    33→
    34→---
    35→
    36→## Route Groups
    37→
    38→### Next.js Route Group Structure
    39→
    40→```
    41→app/
    42→├── (auth)/              # Auth pages - no auth required
    43→├── (dashboard)/         # Protected dashboard - auth required
    44→├── (admin)/             # Super Admin panel - admin role required
    45→├── menu/                # Public menu pages - no auth required
    46→├── r/                   # Restaurant landing pages - no auth required
    47→├── api/                 # API endpoints
    48→├── auth/                # Auth callbacks
    49→├── features/            # Public features page
    50→├── pricing/             # Public pricing page
    51→└── page.tsx             # Landing page
    52→```
    53→
    54→---
    55→
    56→## Public Routes
    57→
    58→These routes are accessible without authentication.
    59→
    60→| Route | File | Description | SEO |
    61→|-------|------|-------------|-----|
    62→| `/` | `app/page.tsx` | Landing page (awwwards-level design) | Yes |
    63→| `/features` | `app/features/page.tsx` | Features showcase | Yes |
    64→| `/pricing` | `app/pricing/page.tsx` | Pricing plans comparison | Yes |
    65→| `/menu/[slug]` | `app/menu/[slug]/page.tsx` | Public menu (QR code target) | ISR |
    66→| `/r/[slug]` | `app/r/[slug]/page.tsx` | Restaurant landing page | Yes |
    67→
    68→### Key Public Route: `/menu/[slug]`
    69→
    70→This is the **most important route** in the platform - the QR code target.
    71→
    72→- **Purpose**: Display restaurant menu to customers
    73→- **URL Pattern**: `https://e-menum.net/menu/{restaurant-slug}`
    74→- **Query Parameters**:
    75→  - `?table_id={uuid}` - Table identification for waiter calls
    76→- **Rendering**: ISR (Incremental Static Regeneration) with revalidation on publish
    77→- **Performance Target**: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1
    78→
    79→---
    80→
    81→## Auth Routes
    82→
    83→Authentication routes handled by the `(auth)` route group.
    84→
    85→| Route | File | Description |
    86→|-------|------|-------------|
    87→| `/login` | `app/(auth)/login/page.tsx` | User login form |
    88→| `/register` | `app/(auth)/register/page.tsx` | Merchant registration |
    89→| `/password-recovery` | `app/(auth)/password-recovery/page.tsx` | Password reset request |
    90→| `/reset-password` | `app/(auth)/reset-password/page.tsx` | Password reset form |
    91→| `/verify-email` | `app/(auth)/verify-email/page.tsx` | Email verification |
    92→| `/auth/callback` | `app/auth/callback/route.ts` | OAuth callback handler |
    93→
    94→### Auth Flow
    95→
    96→```
    97→1. Register → /register
    98→2. Email verification sent → /verify-email
    99→3. Click link in email → /auth/callback
   100→4. Login → /login
   101→5. Forgot password → /password-recovery → /reset-password
   102→```
   103→
   104→---
   105→
   106→## Dashboard Routes (Protected)
   107→
   108→Protected routes requiring authentication. Access controlled by organization membership and role.
   109→
   110→| Route | File | Description | Min Role |
   111→|-------|------|-------------|----------|
   112→| `/dashboard` | `app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx` | Main dashboard, QR access | Viewer |
   113→| `/products` | `app/(dashboard)/products/page.tsx` | Product management | Manager |
   114→| `/products/new` | `app/(dashboard)/products/new/page.tsx` | Add new product | Manager |
   115→| `/products/[id]` | `app/(dashboard)/products/[id]/page.tsx` | Edit product | Manager |
   116→| `/categories` | `app/(dashboard)/categories/page.tsx` | Category management | Manager |
   117→| `/tables` | `app/(dashboard)/tables/page.tsx` | Table QR management | Manager |
   118→| `/waiter` | `app/(dashboard)/waiter/page.tsx` | Waiter call panel (realtime) | Waiter |
   119→| `/audit` | `app/(dashboard)/audit/page.tsx` | Audit log viewer | Admin |
   120→| `/settings` | `app/(dashboard)/settings/page.tsx` | Organization settings | Admin |
   121→
   122→### Role Hierarchy
   123→
   124→```
   125→Owner > Admin > Manager > Waiter > Viewer
   126→```
   127→
   128→| Role | Permissions |
   129→|------|-------------|
   130→| Owner | Full access, billing, delete organization |
   131→| Admin | Settings, audit, team management |
   132→| Manager | Products, categories, tables |
   133→| Waiter | Waiter panel, view dashboard |
   134→| Viewer | Read-only dashboard access |
   135→
   136→---
   137→
   138→## Admin Routes (Super Admin Only)
   139→
   140→Super Admin panel for platform management. Requires `super_admin` role.
   141→
   142→| Route | File | Description |
   143→|-------|------|-------------|
   144→| `/admin` | `app/(admin)/admin/page.tsx` | Admin dashboard overview |
   145→| `/admin/organizations` | `app/(admin)/admin/organizations/page.tsx` | Tenant management |
   146→| `/admin/plans` | `app/(admin)/admin/plans/page.tsx` | Plan/feature management |
   147→| `/admin/overrides` | `app/(admin)/admin/overrides/page.tsx` | Feature overrides (ABAC) |
   148→| `/admin/ai` | `app/(admin)/admin/ai/page.tsx` | AI token management |
   149→
   150→### Admin Capabilities
   151→
   152→- Activate/deactivate tenants
   153→- Assign subscription plans
   154→- Create feature overrides with expiration
   155→- Impersonate users (audit logged)
   156→- Export compliance data
   157→- Manage AI quotas
   158→
   159→---
   160→
   161→## API Routes
   162→
   163→Backend API endpoints for frontend interactions.
   164→
   165→### Authentication
   166→
   167→| Route | Method | Description |
   168→|-------|--------|-------------|
   169→| `/api/auth/logout` | POST | Sign out user |
   170→
   171→### Locations
   172→
   173→| Route | Method | Description |
   174→|-------|--------|-------------|
   175→| `/api/locations` | GET | List locations |
   176→| `/api/locations` | POST | Create location |
   177→| `/api/locations/[id]` | GET | Get single location |
   178→| `/api/locations/[id]` | PUT | Update location |
   179→| `/api/locations/[id]` | DELETE | Delete location |
   180→
   181→### Menu Operations
   182→
   183→| Route | Method | Description |
   184→|-------|--------|-------------|
   185→| `/api/menu/publish` | POST | Publish menu (creates snapshot) |
   186→| `/api/menu/snapshot` | GET | Get menu snapshot with hash |
   187→
   188→### QR Generation
   189→
   190→| Route | Method | Description |
   191→|-------|--------|-------------|
   192→| `/api/qr/generate` | POST | Generate QR codes (SVG, PNG, PDF) |
   193→
   194→### Service Requests
   195→
   196→| Route | Method | Description |
   197→|-------|--------|-------------|
   198→| `/api/service-request` | POST | Create waiter call request |
   199→
   200→### API Response Format
   201→
   202→All API responses follow a consistent format:
   203→
   204→```typescript
   205→// Success
   206→{
   207→  "success": true,
   208→  "data": { ... }
   209→}
   210→
   211→// Error
   212→{
   213→  "success": false,
   214→  "error": {
   215→    "code": "ERROR_CODE",
   216→    "message": "Human readable message"
   217→  }
   218→}
   219→```
   220→
   221→---
   222→
   223→## Route Patterns
   224→
   225→### Dynamic Routes
   226→
   227→| Pattern | Example | Usage |
   228→|---------|---------|-------|
   229→| `[slug]` | `/menu/kebapci-mehmet` | Restaurant identifier |
   230→| `[id]` | `/products/uuid-here` | Resource ID |

   233→
   234→- `(auth)` - Parentheses indicate route group (not in URL)

   264→1. Check for valid Supabase session

1→/**
     2→ * Rate Limiter Service - Dual Storage Strategy
     3→ *
     4→ * This service implements rate limiting for API endpoints using two strategies:
     5→ * 1. Database-backed (Supabase) for authenticated users - persistent across instances
     6→ * 2. In-memory (Map) for IP-based limits - fast, temporary tracking
     7→ *
     8→ * Features:
     9→ * - Configurable request limits and time windows
    10→ * - Automatic cleanup of expired entries (in-memory)
    11→ * - Turkish error messages for consistency
    12→ * - Result types for type-safe error handling
    13→ *
    14→ * Usage:
    15→ * - For authenticated endpoints: Use user ID as identifier with database strategy
    16→ * - For public endpoints: Use IP address as identifier with memory strategy
    17→ *
    18→ * @example
    19→ * // Check rate limit for authenticated user
    20→ * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('user-123', 20, 60000, 'database')
    21→ * if (!result.allowed) {
    22→ *   return NextResponse.json({ error: result.error }, { status: 429 })
    23→ * }
    24→ *
    25→ * // Check rate limit for IP address
    26→ * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('192.168.1.1', 10, 60000, 'memory')
    27→ */
    28→
    29→import { createServerSupabaseClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'
    30→
    31→/**
    32→ * Storage strategy for rate limiting
    33→ * - database: Persistent storage in Supabase for authenticated users
    34→ * - memory: In-memory Map for IP-based limits (faster, temporary)
    35→ */
    36→export type RateLimitStrategy = 'database' | 'memory'
    37→
    38→/**
    39→ * Result of rate limit check
    40→ */
    41→export interface RateLimitResult {
    42→  /** Whether the request is allowed */
    43→  allowed: boolean
    44→  /** Current request count in the window */
    45→  currentCount: number
    46→  /** Maximum allowed requests */
    47→  limit: number
    48→  /** Time remaining in milliseconds until reset */
    49→  resetIn: number
    50→  /** Error message if not allowed (in Turkish) */
    51→  error?: string
    52→  /** Timestamp when the rate limit window resets */
    53→  resetAt: Date
    54→}
    55→
    56→/**
    57→ * Result of reset operation
    58→ */
    59→export interface ResetLimitResult {
    60→  /** Whether the operation succeeded */
    61→  success: boolean
    62→  /** Error message if operation failed */
    63→  error?: string
    64→}
    65→
    66→/**
    67→ * In-memory rate limit entry
    68→ */
    69→interface RateLimitEntry {
    70→  /** Number of requests made in current window */
    71→  count: number
    72→  /** Timestamp when the window started */
    73→  windowStart: number
    74→  /** Window duration in milliseconds */
    75→  windowDuration: number
    76→}
    77→
    78→/**
    79→ * Rate Limiter Service
    80→ *
    81→ * Provides rate limiting functionality with dual storage strategy.
    82→ * Automatically cleans up expired entries from in-memory storage.
    83→ */
    84→export class RateLimiterService {
    85→  /** In-memory storage for IP-based rate limits */
    86→  private memoryStore: Map<string, RateLimitEntry> = new Map()
    87→
    88→  /** Cleanup interval ID for automatic expired entry removal */
    89→  private cleanupIntervalId?: NodeJS.Timeout
    90→
    91→  /** Cleanup interval in milliseconds (default: 5 minutes) */
    92→  private readonly CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000
    93→
    94→  constructor() {
    95→    // Start automatic cleanup of expired entries
    96→    this.startCleanup()
    97→  }
    98→
    99→  /**
   100→   * Check if request is allowed within rate limit
   101→   *
   102→   * @param identifier - User ID (for database) or IP address (for memory)
   103→   * @param limit - Maximum number of requests allowed in window
   104→   * @param windowMs - Time window in milliseconds
   105→   * @param strategy - Storage strategy to use ('database' or 'memory')
   106→   * @returns Promise<RateLimitResult> - Rate limit check result
   107→   *
   108→   * @example
   109→   * ```typescript
   110→   * // Check user rate limit (20 requests per minute)
   111→   * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('user-123', 20, 60000, 'database')
   112→   *
   113→   * // Check IP rate limit (10 requests per minute)
   114→   * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('192.168.1.1', 10, 60000, 'memory')
   115→   * ```
   116→   */
   117→  async checkRateLimit(
   118→    identifier: string,
   119→    limit: number,
   120→    windowMs: number,
   121→    strategy: RateLimitStrategy = 'memory'
   122→  ): Promise<RateLimitResult> {
   123→    if (strategy === 'database') {
   124→      return this.checkDatabaseRateLimit(identifier, limit, windowMs)
   125→    } else {
   126→      return this.checkMemoryRateLimit(identifier, limit, windowMs)
   127→    }
   128→  }
   129→
   130→  /**
   131→   * Reset rate limit for an identifier
   132→   *
   133→   * @param identifier - User ID or IP address to reset
   134→   * @param strategy - Storage strategy to use ('database' or 'memory')
   135→   * @returns Promise<ResetLimitResult> - Reset operation result
   136→   *
   137→   * @example
   138→   * ```typescript
   139→   * await rateLimiter.resetLimit('user-123', 'database')
   140→   * ```
   141→   */
   142→  async resetLimit(
   143→    identifier: string,
   144→    strategy: RateLimitStrategy = 'memory'
   145→  ): Promise<ResetLimitResult> {
   146→    try {
   147→      if (strategy === 'database') {

   171→        error: 'Rate limit sifirlama sirasinda hata olustu',
   172→      }
   173→    }
   174→  }
   175→
   176→  /**
   177→   * Check rate limit using database storage (Supabase)
   178→   *
   179→   * @private
   180→   */
   181→  private async checkDatabaseRateLimit(
   182→    identifier: string,
   183→    limit: number,
   184→    windowMs: number
   185→  ): Promise<RateLimitResult> {
   186→    try {

     7→/**
     8→ * Menu Publish API Route Handler
     9→ *
    10→ * This route handles menu publishing by:
    11→ * 1. Authenticating the user and verifying organization access
    12→ * 2. Creating an immutable menu snapshot with SHA-256 hash
    13→ * 3. Triggering ISR revalidation for the public menu page
    14→ *
    15→ * POST /api/menu/publish
    16→ *
    17→ * Request body:
    18→ * {
    19→ *   organizationId: string (required) - Organization UUID to publish
    20→ * }
    21→ *
    22→ * Response:
    23→ * {
    24→ *   success: boolean
    25→ *   data?: {
    26→ *     snapshotId: string - Created snapshot UUID
    27→ *     version: number - Snapshot version number
    28→ *     hash: string - SHA-256 hash for integrity verification
    29→ *     publishedAt: string - ISO timestamp of publish
    30→ *   }
    31→ *   error?: string
    32→ * }
    33→ *
    34→ * Features:
    35→ * - Rate limiting: 30-second cooldown between publishes per organization
    36→ * - Role-based access: Only owner, admin, and manager can publish
    37→ * - Atomic snapshot creation with integrity verification
    38→ */

    40→/**
    41→ * Create Supabase server client with cookie handling
    42→ */
    43→async function createSupabaseClient() {
    44→  const cookieStore = await cookies()
    45→  return createServerClient(

    47→    process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!,
    48→    {
    49→      cookies: {
    50→        getAll() {

    52→        },
    53→        setAll(cookiesToSet) {
    54→          try {
    55→            cookiesToSet.forEach(({ name, value, options }) =>

    58→          } catch {

1→# e-menum.net API Documentation
     2→
     3→This document provides detailed documentation for the e-menum.net API endpoints, including authentication requirements, request/response formats, rate limiting, and error handling.
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Table of Contents
     8→
     9→- [Overview](#overview)
    10→- [Authentication](#authentication)
    11→- [Rate Limiting](#rate-limiting)
    12→- [API Endpoints](#api-endpoints)
    13→  - [Authentication Endpoints](#authentication-endpoints)
    14→  - [Location Endpoints](#location-endpoints)
    15→  - [Menu Endpoints](#menu-endpoints)
    16→  - [QR Generation Endpoints](#qr-generation-endpoints)
    17→  - [Service Request Endpoints](#service-request-endpoints)
    18→- [Response Format](#response-format)
    19→- [Error Handling](#error-handling)
    20→- [Best Practices](#best-practices)
    21→
    22→---
    23→
    24→## Overview
    25→
    26→The e-menum.net API is a RESTful API built with Next.js App Router. All API endpoints follow consistent patterns for authentication, error handling, and response formatting.
    27→
    28→**Base URL:**
    29→- Production: `https://e-menum.net/api`
    30→- Development: `http://localhost:3000/api`
    31→
    32→**Content Type:** All requests and responses use `application/json`
    33→
    34→---
    35→
    36→## Authentication
    37→
    38→Most API endpoints require authentication via Supabase session cookies. Authentication is handled automatically by the browser for authenticated users.
    39→
    40→**Authentication Methods:**
    41→- Session-based authentication (Supabase Auth)
    42→- Automatic session management via cookies
    43→
    44→**Protected Endpoints:**
    45→- All endpoints except `/api/auth/logout` require valid authentication
    46→- Organization-specific endpoints require active organization membership
    47→
    48→---
    49→
    50→## Rate Limiting
    51→
    52→To prevent abuse and ensure fair resource usage, the API implements rate limiting on sensitive endpoints. Rate limits are enforced per user (for authenticated endpoints) or per IP address (for public endpoints).
    53→
    54→### Rate-Limited Endpoints
    55→
    56→| Endpoint | Method | Rate Limit | Identifier | Notes |
    57→|----------|--------|------------|------------|-------|
    58→| `/api/qr/generate` | POST | 1 request per 10 seconds | User ID | CPU-intensive QR code generation |
    59→| `/api/locations` | POST | 1 request per 60 seconds | User ID | Prevents spam organization creation |
    60→| `/api/menu/publish` | POST | 1 request per 30 seconds | Organization ID | Database-intensive snapshot creation |
    61→| `/api/auth/logout` | POST | 10 requests per minute | IP Address | Prevents logout endpoint abuse |
    62→| `/api/service-request` | POST | 1 request per 30 seconds | Table ID | Prevents waiter call spam |
    63→
    64→### Rate Limit Response Headers
    65→
    66→When a rate limit is enforced, the following headers are included in the response:
    67→
    68→```
    69→X-RateLimit-Limit: 10
    70→X-RateLimit-Remaining: 5
    71→X-RateLimit-Reset: 1673234567
    72→```
    73→
    74→### 429 Rate Limit Exceeded Response
    75→
    76→When a rate limit is exceeded, the API returns a `429 Too Many Requests` status code:
    77→
    78→```json
    79→{
    80→  "success": false,
    81→  "error": {
    82→    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    83→    "message": "Lütfen 10 saniye bekleyiniz."
    84→  }
    85→}
    86→```
    87→
    88→**Error Message Format:**
    89→- Turkish language for user-facing messages
    90→- Includes remaining cooldown time in seconds
    91→- Clear indication of when the request can be retried
    92→
    93→### Rate Limit Strategy
    94→
    95→The API uses two rate limiting strategies:
    96→
    97→1. **Database-backed (for authenticated users):**
    98→   - Tracks rate limits using timestamp columns in the database
    99→   - Provides persistent rate limiting across server restarts
   100→   - Used for user-specific and organization-specific limits
   101→
   102→2. **In-memory (for IP-based limits):**
   103→   - Uses in-memory Map for IP address tracking
   104→   - Automatic cleanup after expiration
   105→   - Used for public endpoints like logout
   106→
   107→### Best Practices for Rate Limits
   108→
   109→**For Client Applications:**
   110→
   111→1. **Handle 429 Responses Gracefully:**
   112→   ```typescript
   113→   try {
   114→     const response = await fetch('/api/qr/generate', { method: 'POST', body: data });
   115→
   116→     if (response.status === 429) {
   117→       const error = await response.json();
   118→       // Display error.error.message to user
   119→       // Wait before retrying
   120→       return;
   121→     }
   122→
   123→     const result = await response.json();
   124→     // Handle success
   125→   } catch (error) {
   126→     // Handle network errors
   127→   }
   128→   ```
   129→
   130→2. **Implement Client-Side Throttling:**
   131→   - Disable buttons after submission
   132→   - Show visual feedback during cooldown
   133→   - Cache results when possible
   134→
   135→3. **Respect Rate Limit Headers:**
   136→   - Check `X-RateLimit-Remaining` before making requests
   137→   - Use `X-RateLimit-Reset` to calculate wait time
   138→   - Implement exponential backoff for retries
   139→
   140→4. **Display User Feedback:**
   141→   - Show remaining cooldown time in UI
   142→   - Disable action buttons during cooldown
   143→   - Provide clear error messages
   144→
   145→---
   146→
   147→## API Endpoints
   148→
   149→### Authentication Endpoints
   150→
   151→#### POST /api/auth/logout
   152→
   153→Signs out the current user and clears the session.
   154→
   155→**Rate Limit:** 10 requests per minute per IP address
   156→
   157→**Authentication:** Not required (public endpoint)
   158→
   159→**Request:**
   160→```http
   161→POST /api/auth/logout
   162→Content-Type: application/json
   163→```
   164→
   165→**Response (200 OK):**
   166→```json
   167→{
   168→  "success": true,
   169→  "data": {
   170→    "message": "Çıkış başarılı"
   171→  }
   172→}
   173→```
   174→
   175→**Rate Limit Response (429):**
   176→```json
   177→{
   178→  "success": false,
   179→  "error": {
   180→    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
   181→    "message": "Çok fazla istek gönderdiniz. Lütfen 45 saniye bekleyiniz."
   182→  }
   183→}
   184→```
   185→
   186→---
   187→
   188→### Location Endpoints
   189→
   190→#### POST /api/locations
   191→
   192→Creates a new organization (location). This endpoint is used during the onboarding process.
   193→
   194→**Rate Limit:** 1 request per 60 seconds per user
   195→
   196→**Authentication:** Required
   197→
   198→**Request:**
   199→```http
   200→POST /api/locations
   201→Content-Type: application/json
   202→
   203→{
   204→  "name": "Kebapçı Mehmet",
   205→  "slug": "kebapci-mehmet",
   206→  "description": "Geleneksel Türk mutfağı",
   207→  "address": "Atatürk Caddesi No:123, İzmir",
   208→  "phone": "+90 232 123 4567"
   209→}
   210→```
   211→
   212→**Response (201 Created):**
   213→```json
   214→{
   215→  "success": true,
   216→  "data": {
   217→    "id": "uuid-here",
   218→    "name": "Kebapçı Mehmet",
   219→    "slug": "kebapci-mehmet",
   220→    "created_at": "2025-01-14T12:00:00Z"
   221→  }
   222→}
   223→```
   224→
   225→**Rate Limit Response (429):**
   226→```json
   227→{
   228→  "success": false,
   229→  "error": {
   230→    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
   231→    "message": "Lütfen 45 saniye bekleyiniz."
   232→  }
   233→}
   234→```
   235→
   236→**Notes:**
   237→- Rate limit prevents spam organization creation
   238→- Users can create one organization per minute
   239→- Cooldown is tracked per user ID
   240→
   241→---
   242→
   243→### Menu Endpoints
   244→
   245→#### POST /api/menu/publish
   246→
   247→Publishes the current menu by creating a snapshot. This triggers menu regeneration and invalidates caches.
   248→
   249→**Rate Limit:** 1 request per 30 seconds per organization
   250→

    89→### 3. withRateLimit Middleware Not Used - Architecture Violation

    91→**Problem**: The `withRateLimit()` middleware helper was created in `lib/middleware/rate-limit.ts` but is NOT used in any endpoint. Instead, each endpoint implements its own custom rate limiting logic. This violates DRY principles and makes the code harder to maintain.

   105→export async function POST(request: NextRequest) {

   141→

   145→// Wrap handler with rate limiting middleware

1→/**
     2→ * Rate Limit Middleware Helper
     3→ *
     4→ * Provides a higher-order function to wrap API route handlers with rate limiting.
     5→ * Supports both authenticated (user ID) and unauthenticated (IP-based) rate limiting.
     6→ *
     7→ * Features:
     8→ * - Flexible identifier extraction (user ID, IP, custom)
     9→ * - Automatic strategy selection (database for user IDs, memory for IPs)
    10→ * - Turkish error messages for consistency
    11→ * - Type-safe with TypeScript
    12→ *
    13→ * Usage:
    14→ * ```typescript
    15→ * // Authenticated endpoint (user ID-based)
    16→ * export const POST = withRateLimit(
    17→ *   async (request, context) => {
    18→ *     // Your handler logic
    19→ *   },
    20→ *   {
    21→ *     limit: 20,
    22→ *     windowMs: 60000, // 1 minute
    23→ *     identifierType: 'user',
    24→ *   }
    25→ * )
    26→ *
    27→ * // Public endpoint (IP-based)
    28→ * export const POST = withRateLimit(
    29→ *   async (request) => {
    30→ *     // Your handler logic
    31→ *   },
    32→ *   {
    33→ *     limit: 10,
    34→ *     windowMs: 60000,
    35→ *     identifierType: 'ip',
    36→ *   }
    37→ * )
    38→ *
    39→ * // Custom identifier extraction
    40→ * export const POST = withRateLimit(
    41→ *   async (request) => {
    42→ *     // Your handler logic
    43→ *   },
    44→ *   {
    45→ *     limit: 5,
    46→ *     windowMs: 3600000, // 1 hour
    47→ *     identifierType: 'custom',
    48→ *     getIdentifier: async (request) => {
    49→ *       const body = await request.json()
    50→ *       return body.organizationId
    51→ *     },
    52→ *   }
    53→ * )
    54→ * ```
    55→ */
    56→
    57→import { NextRequest, NextResponse } from 'next/server'
    58→import { rateLimiter, type RateLimitStrategy } from '@/lib/services/rate-limiter'
    59→import { createServerSupabaseClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'
    60→
    61→/**
    62→ * Rate limit configuration options
    63→ */
    64→export interface RateLimitOptions {
    65→  /** Maximum number of requests allowed in the window */
    66→  limit: number
    67→
    68→  /** Time window in milliseconds */
    69→  windowMs: number
    70→
    71→  /**
    72→   * Type of identifier to use for rate limiting
    73→   * - 'user': Extract authenticated user ID (requires auth, uses database strategy)
    74→   * - 'ip': Extract client IP address (uses memory strategy)
    75→   * - 'custom': Use custom identifier extraction function
    76→   */
    77→  identifierType: 'user' | 'ip' | 'custom'
    78→
    79→  /**
    80→   * Custom identifier extraction function
    81→   * Required when identifierType is 'custom'
    82→   * Should return a unique identifier string for rate limiting
    83→   */
    84→  getIdentifier?: (request: NextRequest) => Promise<string | null>
    85→
    86→  /**
    87→   * Override the automatic strategy selection
    88→   * By default: 'database' for user IDs, 'memory' for IPs
    89→   */
    90→  strategy?: RateLimitStrategy
    91→
    92→  /**
    93→   * Custom error message to return when rate limited
    94→   * Default: "Cok fazla istek. Lutfen {seconds} saniye bekleyin"
    95→   */
    96→  errorMessage?: string
    97→}
    98→
    99→/**
   100→ * API route handler type
   101→ * Matches Next.js App Router API route handler signature
   102→ */
   103→export type APIRouteHandler<T = unknown> = (
   104→  request: NextRequest,
   105→  context?: T
   106→) => Promise<NextResponse> | NextResponse
   107→
   108→/**
   109→ * Extract client IP address from request
   110→ *
   111→ * Attempts to extract IP from various headers in order of trustworthiness:
   112→ * 1. x-real-ip (set by reverse proxies)
   113→ * 2. x-forwarded-for (may contain multiple IPs, takes first)
   114→ * 3. request.ip (Next.js provided IP)
   115→ *
   116→ * @param request - Next.js request object
   117→ * @returns IP address string or 'unknown' if not found
   118→ */
   119→function getClientIP(request: NextRequest): string {
   120→  // Check x-real-ip header (commonly set by Nginx)
   121→  const realIP = request.headers.get('x-real-ip')
   122→  if (realIP) {
   123→    return realIP
   124→  }
   125→
   126→  // Check x-forwarded-for header (may contain multiple IPs)
   127→  const forwardedFor = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for')
   128→  if (forwardedFor) {
   129→    // Take the first IP in the list (client IP)
   130→    const ips = forwardedFor.split(',').map((ip) => ip.trim())
   131→    if (ips[0]) {
   132→      return ips[0]
   133→    }
   134→  }
   135→
   136→  // Fallback to Next.js provided IP
   137→  return request.ip || 'unknown'
   138→}
   139→
   140→/**
   141→ * Extract authenticated user ID from Supabase session
   142→ *
   143→ * @param request - Next.js request object
   144→ * @returns User ID string or null if not authenticated
   145→ */
   146→async function getUserID(request: NextRequest): Promise<string | null> {
   147→  try {
   148→    const supabase = await createServerSupabaseClient()
   149→    const {
   150→      data: { user },
   151→    } = await supabase.auth.getUser()
   152→
   153→    return user?.id || null
   154→  } catch {
   155→    return null
   156→  }
   157→}
   158→
   159→/**
   160→ * Higher-order function that wraps API route handlers with rate limiting
   161→ *
   162→ * @param handler - The API route handler to wrap
   163→ * @param options - Rate limit configuration options
   164→ * @returns Wrapped API route handler with rate limiting
   165→ *
   166→ * @example
   167→ * ```typescript
   168→ * export const POST = withRateLimit(
   169→ *   async (request) => {
   170→ *     return NextResponse.json({ success: true })
   171→ *   },
   172→ *   {
   173→ *     limit: 20,
   174→ *     windowMs: 60000, // 1 minute
   175→ *     identifierType: 'user',
   176→ *   }
   177→ * )
   178→ * ```
   179→ */
   180→export function withRateLimit<T = unknown>(
   181→  handler: APIRouteHandler<T>,
   182→  options: RateLimitOptions
   183→): APIRouteHandler<T> {
   184→  return async (request: NextRequest, context?: T) => {
   185→    try {
   186→      // Extract identifier based on type
   187→      let identifier: string | null = null
   188→
   189→      if (options.identifierType === 'user') {
   190→        identifier = await getUserID(request)
   191→
   192→        // If user ID required but not found, return 401
   193→        if (!identifier) {
   194→          return NextResponse.json(
   195→            { success: false, error: 'Oturum acmaniz gerekiyor' },
   196→            { status: 401 }
   197→          )
   198→        }
   199→      } else if (options.identifierType === 'ip') {
   200→        identifier = getClientIP(request)
   201→      } else if (options.identifierType === 'custom') {
   202→        if (!options.getIdentifier) {
   203→          throw new Error(
   204→            'getIdentifier function required for custom identifier type'
   205→          )
   206→        }
   207→        identifier = await options.getIdentifier(request)
   208→      }
   209→
   210→      // If identifier is null or 'unknown', fail open (allow request)
   211→      if (!identifier || identifier === 'unknown') {
   212→        return handler(request, context)
   213→      }
   214→
   215→      // Determine strategy
   216→      const strategy: RateLimitStrategy =
   217→        options.strategy ||
   218→        (options.identifierType === 'user' ? 'database' : 'memory')
   219→
   220→      // Check rate limit
   221→      const rateLimitResult = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit(
   222→        identifier,
   223→        options.limit,
   224→        options.windowMs,
   225→        strategy
   226→      )
   227→
   228→      // If rate limit exceeded, return 429
   229→      if (!rateLimitResult.allowed) {
   230→        const errorMessage =
   231→          options.errorMessage || rateLimitResult.error || 'Cok fazla istek'
   232→
   233→        return NextResponse.json(
   234→          {
   235→            success: false,
   236→            error: errorMessage,
   237→            retryAfter: Math.ceil(rateLimitResult.resetIn / 1000),
   238→          },
   239→          {
   240→            status: 429,
   241→            headers: {
   242→              'Retry-After': Math.ceil(rateLimitResult.resetIn / 1000).toString(),
   243→              'X-RateLimit-Limit': rateLimitResult.limit.toString(),
   244→              'X-RateLimit-Remaining': '0',
   245→              'X-RateLimit-Reset': rateLimitResult.resetAt.toISOString(),
   246→            },
   247→          }
   248→        )
   249→      }
   250→
   251→      // Rate limit not exceeded - add rate limit headers and call handler
   252→      const response = await handler(request, context)
   253→
   254→      // Add rate limit headers to successful response
   255→      response.headers.set(
   256→        'X-RateLimit-Limit',
   257→        rateLimitResult.limit.toString()
   258→      )
   259→      response.headers.set(
   260→        'X-RateLimit-Remaining',
   261→        Math.max(0, rateLimitResult.limit - rateLimitResult.currentCount).toString()
   262→      )
   263→      response.headers.set(
   264→        'X-RateLimit-Reset',
   265→        rateLimitResult.resetAt.toISOString()
   266→      )
   267→
   268→      return response
   269→    } catch (error) {
   270→      // On any error, fail open (allow request to proceed)
   271→      // Log error in production for monitoring
   272→      return handler(request, context)
   273→    }
   274→  }
   275→}

## 🎉 QA Fixes Complete!

All **5 critical and major issues** identified by the QA reviewer have been successfully addressed and committed.

### ✅ Issues Fixed

#### 1. **Missing rate_limits Database Table** (CRITICAL)
- **Problem**: RateLimiterService referenced a table that didn't exist
- **Fix**: Added complete table definition to `supabase/migrations/008_rate_limiting.sql`
- **Includes**: Primary key, indexes, and proper column types for rate limiting

#### 2. **Rate Limit Intervals Don't Match Specification** (CRITICAL)
- **Problem**: Intervals were incorrectly configured, especially locations (12x too lenient!)
- **Fixes**:
  - QR generation: `10s → 3s` (20 requests/minute) ✓
  - Location creation: `60s → 3600s` (5 requests/hour) ✓
  - Menu publishing: `30s → 6s` (10 requests/minute) ✓

#### 3. **withRateLimit Middleware Not Used** (CRITICAL - Architecture Violation)
- **Problem**: Created middleware was completely unused; endpoints had custom implementations
- **Fix**: Refactored all 4 endpoints to use the middleware:
  - `/api/auth/logout` → Uses `rateLimitPresets.publicEndpoint`
  - `/api/qr/generate` → User-based, 20 req/min
  - `/api/locations` → User-based, 5 req/hour
  - `/api/menu/publish` → Organization-based with custom identifier

#### 4. **Inconsistent Rate Limiting Patterns** (MAJOR)
- **Problem**: Each endpoint used different rate limiting approach
- **Fix**: All endpoints now use consistent `withRateLimit` middleware pattern

#### 5. **Migration Incomplete** (MAJOR)
- **Problem**: Migration only added one column, missing the rate_limits table
- **Fix**: Migration now creates both structures needed for rate limiting

### 📊 Impact

**Code Quality:**
- **-62 net lines** (101 additions, 163 deletions) - cleaner, more maintainable code
- **DRY principle restored** - no more duplicated rate limiting logic
- **Consistent architecture** - all endpoints follow same pattern

**Functionality:**
- ✅ Rate limits now match specification requirements
- ✅ Rate limit headers included in responses (`X-RateLimit-*`)
- ✅ Database-backed and memory-based strategies working
- ✅ Proper fail-open error handling maintained

    23→
    24→## Overview
    25→
    26→The e-menum.net API is a RESTful API built with Next.js App Router. All API endpoints follow consistent patterns for authentication, error handling, and response formatting.
    27→
    28→**Base URL:**
    29→- Production: `https://e-menum.net/api`
    30→- Development: `http://localhost:3000/api`
    31→
    32→**Content Type:** All requests and responses use `application/json`
    33→
    34→---
    35→
    36→## Authentication
    37→
    38→Most API endpoints require authentication via Supabase session cookies. Authentication is handled automatically by the browser for authenticated users.
    39→
    40→**Authentication Methods:**
    41→- Session-based authentication (Supabase Auth)
    42→- Automatic session management via cookies
    43→
    44→**Protected Endpoints:**
    45→- All endpoints except `/api/auth/logout` require valid authentication
    46→- Organization-specific endpoints require active organization membership
    47→
    48→---
    49→
    50→## Rate Limiting
    51→
    52→To prevent abuse and ensure fair resource usage, the API implements rate limiting on sensitive endpoints. Rate limits are enforced per user (for authenticated endpoints) or per IP address (for public endpoints).
    53→
    54→### Rate-Limited Endpoints
    55→
    56→| Endpoint | Method | Rate Limit | Identifier | Notes |
    57→|----------|--------|------------|------------|-------|
    58→| `/api/qr/generate` | POST | 1 request per 10 seconds | User ID | CPU-intensive QR code generation |
    59→| `/api/locations` | POST | 1 request per 60 seconds | User ID | Prevents spam organization creation |
    60→| `/api/menu/publish` | POST | 1 request per 30 seconds | Organization ID | Database-intensive snapshot creation |
    61→| `/api/auth/logout` | POST | 10 requests per minute | IP Address | Prevents logout endpoint abuse |
    62→| `/api/service-request` | POST | 1 request per 30 seconds | Table ID | Prevents waiter call spam |
    63→
    64→### Rate Limit Response Headers
    65→
    66→When a rate limit is enforced, the following headers are included in the response:
    67→
    68→```
    69→X-RateLimit-Limit: 10
    70→X-RateLimit-Remaining: 5
    71→X-RateLimit-Reset: 1673234567
    72→```
    73→
    74→### 429 Rate Limit Exceeded Response
    75→
    76→When a rate limit is exceeded, the API returns a `429 Too Many Requests` status code:
    77→
    78→```json
    79→{
    80→  "success": false,
    81→  "error": {
    82→    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    83→    "message": "Lütfen 10 saniye bekleyiniz."
    84→  }
    85→}
    86→```

    88→**Error Message Format:**

    90→- Includes remaining cooldown time in seconds
    91→- Clear indication of when the request can be retried
    92→

    95→The API uses two rate limiting strategies:
    96→

    99→   - Provides persistent rate limiting across server restarts

1→# e-menum.net API Documentation
     2→
     3→This document provides detailed documentation for the e-menum.net API endpoints, including authentication requirements, request/response formats, rate limiting, and error handling.
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Table of Contents
     8→
     9→- [Overview](#overview)
    10→- [Authentication](#authentication)
    11→- [Rate Limiting](#rate-limiting)
    12→- [API Endpoints](#api-endpoints)
    13→  - [Authentication Endpoints](#authentication-endpoints)
    14→  - [Location Endpoints](#location-endpoints)
    15→  - [Menu Endpoints](#menu-endpoints)
    16→  - [QR Generation Endpoints](#qr-generation-endpoints)
    17→  - [Service Request Endpoints](#service-request-endpoints)
    18→- [Response Format](#response-format)
    19→- [Error Handling](#error-handling)
    20→- [Best Practices](#best-practices)
    21→
    22→---
    23→
    24→## Overview
    25→
    26→The e-menum.net API is a RESTful API built with Next.js App Router. All API endpoints follow consistent patterns for authentication, error handling, and response formatting.
    27→
    28→**Base URL:**
    29→- Production: `https://e-menum.net/api`
    30→- Development: `http://localhost:3000/api`
    31→
    32→**Content Type:** All requests and responses use `application/json`
    33→
    34→---
    35→
    36→## Authentication
    37→
    38→Most API endpoints require authentication via Supabase session cookies. Authentication is handled automatically by the browser for authenticated users.
    39→
    40→**Authentication Methods:**
    41→- Session-based authentication (Supabase Auth)
    42→- Automatic session management via cookies
    43→
    44→**Protected Endpoints:**
    45→- All endpoints except `/api/auth/logout` require valid authentication
    46→- Organization-specific endpoints require active organization membership
    47→
    48→---
    49→
    50→## Rate Limiting
    51→
    52→To prevent abuse and ensure fair resource usage, the API implements rate limiting on sensitive endpoints. Rate limits are enforced per user (for authenticated endpoints) or per IP address (for public endpoints).
    53→
    54→### Rate-Limited Endpoints
    55→
    56→| Endpoint | Method | Rate Limit | Identifier | Notes |
    57→|----------|--------|------------|------------|-------|
    58→| `/api/qr/generate` | POST | 1 request per 10 seconds | User ID | CPU-intensive QR code generation |
    59→| `/api/locations` | POST | 1 request per 60 seconds | User ID | Prevents spam organization creation |
    60→| `/api/menu/publish` | POST | 1 request per 30 seconds | Organization ID | Database-intensive snapshot creation |
    61→| `/api/auth/logout` | POST | 10 requests per minute | IP Address | Prevents logout endpoint abuse |
    62→| `/api/service-request` | POST | 1 request per 30 seconds | Table ID | Prevents waiter call spam |
    63→
    64→### Rate Limit Response Headers
    65→
    66→When a rate limit is enforced, the following headers are included in the response:
    67→
    68→```
    69→X-RateLimit-Limit: 10
    70→X-RateLimit-Remaining: 5
    71→X-RateLimit-Reset: 1673234567
    72→```
    73→
    74→### 429 Rate Limit Exceeded Response
    75→
    76→When a rate limit is exceeded, the API returns a `429 Too Many Requests` status code:
    77→
    78→```json
    79→{
    80→  "success": false,
    81→  "error": {
    82→    "code": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
    83→    "message": "Lütfen 10 saniye bekleyiniz."
    84→  }
    85→}
    86→```
    87→
    88→**Error Message Format:**
    89→- Turkish language for user-facing messages
    90→- Includes remaining cooldown time in seconds
    91→- Clear indication of when the request can be retried
    92→
    93→### Rate Limit Strategy
    94→
    95→The API uses two rate limiting strategies:
    96→
    97→1. **Database-backed (for authenticated users):**
    98→   - Tracks rate limits using timestamp columns in the database
    99→   - Provides persistent rate limiting across server restarts
   100→   - Used for user-specific and organization-specific limits
   101→
   102→2. **In-memory (for IP-based limits):**
   103→   - Uses in-memory Map for IP address tracking
   104→   - Automatic cleanup after expiration
   105→   - Used for public endpoints like logout
   106→
   107→### Best Practices for Rate Limits
   108→
   109→**For Client Applications:**
   110→
   111→1. **Handle 429 Responses Gracefully:**
   112→   ```typescript
   113→   try {
   114→     const response = await fetch('/api/qr/generate', { method: 'POST', body: data });
   115→
   116→     if (response.status === 429) {
   117→       const error = await response.json();
   118→       // Display error.error.message to user
   119→       // Wait before retrying
   120→       return;
   121→     }
   122→
   123→     const result = await response.json();
   124→     // Handle success
   125→   } catch (error) {
   126→     // Handle network errors
   127→   }
   128→   ```
   129→
   130→2. **Implement Client-Side Throttling:**
   131→   - Disable buttons after submission
   132→   - Show visual feedback during cooldown
   133→   - Cache results when possible
   134→
   135→3. **Respect Rate Limit Headers:**
   136→   - Check `X-RateLimit-Remaining` before making requests
   137→   - Use `X-RateLimit-Reset` to calculate wait time
   138→   - Implement exponential backoff for retries
   139→
   140→4. **Display User Feedback:**
   141→   - Show remaining cooldown time in UI
   142→   - Disable action buttons during cooldown
   143→   - Provide clear error messages
   144→
   145→---
   146→
   147→## API Endpoints
   148→
   149→### Authentication Endpoints
   150→
   151→#### POST /api/auth/logout
   152→
   153→Signs out the current user and clears the session.
   154→
   155→**Rate Limit:** 10 requests per minute per IP address

     6→ * 2. In-memory (Map) for IP-based limits - fast, temporary tracking

    12→ * - Result types for type-safe error handling
    13→ *
    14→ * Usage:
    15→ * - For authenticated endpoints: Use user ID as identifier with database strategy
    16→ * - For public endpoints: Use IP address as identifier with memory strategy
    17→ *
    18→ * @example

    20→ * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('user-123', 20, 60000, 'database')

    22→ *   return NextResponse.json({ error: result.error }, { status: 429 })

    24→ *
    25→ * // Check rate limit for IP address

    28→
    29→import { createServerSupabaseClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server'
    30→
    31→/**
    32→ * Storage strategy for rate limiting
    33→ * - database: Persistent storage in Supabase for authenticated users
    34→ * - memory: In-memory Map for IP-based limits (faster, temporary)
    35→ */
    36→export type RateLimitStrategy = 'database' | 'memory'
    37→
    38→/**
    39→ * Result of rate limit check
    40→ */
    41→export interface RateLimitResult {
    42→  /** Whether the request is allowed */
    43→  allowed: boolean
    44→  /** Current request count in the window */
    45→  currentCount: number
    46→  /** Maximum allowed requests */
    47→  limit: number
    48→  /** Time remaining in milliseconds until reset */
    49→  resetIn: number
    50→  /** Error message if not allowed (in Turkish) */
    51→  error?: string
    52→  /** Timestamp when the rate limit window resets */
    53→  resetAt: Date
    54→}
    55→
    56→/**
    57→ * Result of reset operation
    58→ */
    59→export interface ResetLimitResult {
    60→  /** Whether the operation succeeded */
    61→  success: boolean
    62→  /** Error message if operation failed */
    63→  error?: string
    64→}
    65→
    66→/**
    67→ * In-memory rate limit entry
    68→ */
    69→interface RateLimitEntry {
    70→  /** Number of requests made in current window */
    71→  count: number
    72→  /** Timestamp when the window started */
    73→  windowStart: number
    74→  /** Window duration in milliseconds */
    75→  windowDuration: number
    76→}
    77→
    78→/**
    79→ * Rate Limiter Service
    80→ *
    81→ * Provides rate limiting functionality with dual storage strategy.
    82→ * Automatically cleans up expired entries from in-memory storage.
    83→ */
    84→export class RateLimiterService {
    85→  /** In-memory storage for IP-based rate limits */
    86→  private memoryStore: Map<string, RateLimitEntry> = new Map()
    87→
    88→  /** Cleanup interval ID for automatic expired entry removal */
    89→  private cleanupIntervalId?: NodeJS.Timeout
    90→
    91→  /** Cleanup interval in milliseconds (default: 5 minutes) */
    92→  private readonly CLEANUP_INTERVAL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000
    93→
    94→  constructor() {
    95→    // Start automatic cleanup of expired entries
    96→    this.startCleanup()
    97→  }
    98→
    99→  /**
   100→   * Check if request is allowed within rate limit
   101→   *
   102→   * @param identifier - User ID (for database) or IP address (for memory)
   103→   * @param limit - Maximum number of requests allowed in window
   104→   * @param windowMs - Time window in milliseconds
   105→   * @param strategy - Storage strategy to use ('database' or 'memory')
   106→   * @returns Promise<RateLimitResult> - Rate limit check result
   107→   *
   108→   * @example
   109→   * ```typescript
   110→   * // Check user rate limit (20 requests per minute)
   111→   * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('user-123', 20, 60000, 'database')
   112→   *
   113→   * // Check IP rate limit (10 requests per minute)
   114→   * const result = await rateLimiter.checkRateLimit('192.168.1.1', 10, 60000, 'memory')
   115→   * ```
   116→   */
   117→  async checkRateLimit(
   118→    identifier: string,
   119→    limit: number,
   120→    windowMs: number,
   121→    strategy: RateLimitStrategy = 'memory'
   122→  ): Promise<RateLimitResult> {
   123→    if (strategy === 'database') {
   124→      return this.checkDatabaseRateLimit(identifier, limit, windowMs)
   125→    } else {
   126→      return this.checkMemoryRateLimit(identifier, limit, windowMs)
   127→    }
   128→  }
   129→
   130→  /**
   131→   * Reset rate limit for an identifier
   132→   *
   133→   * @param identifier - User ID or IP address to reset
   134→   * @param strategy - Storage strategy to use ('database' or 'memory')
   135→   * @returns Promise<ResetLimitResult> - Reset operation result
   136→   *
   137→   * @example
   138→   * ```typescript
   139→   * await rateLimiter.resetLimit('user-123', 'database')
   140→   * ```
   141→   */
   142→  async resetLimit(
   143→    identifier: string,
   144→    strategy: RateLimitStrategy = 'memory'
   145→  ): Promise<ResetLimitResult> {
   146→    try {
   147→      if (strategy === 'database') {

   171→        error: 'Rate limit sifirlama sirasinda hata olustu',
   172→      }
   173→    }
   174→  }
   175→
   176→  /**
   177→   * Check rate limit using database storage (Supabase)
   178→   *
   179→   * @private
   180→   */
   181→  private async checkDatabaseRateLimit(
   182→    identifier: string,
   183→    limit: number,
   184→    windowMs: number
   185→  ): Promise<RateLimitResult> {
   186→    try {

    20→ * Generates QR codes for restaurant menus in various formats.
    21→ * Supports SVG, PNG (1024/2048/4096px), and A5 PDF formats.
    22→ *
    23→ * POST /api/qr/generate
    24→ *
    25→ * Request body:
    26→ * {
    27→ *   slug: string (required) - Organization's menu slug
    28→ *   tableId?: string (optional) - Table UUID for table-specific QR codes
    29→ *   format?: 'SVG' | 'PNG' | 'PDF' | 'ALL' (optional, default: 'ALL')
    30→ *   pngSize?: 1024 | 2048 | 4096 (optional, default: 1024, only for PNG format)
    31→ *   options?: {
    32→ *     title?: string - Title for PDF

    36→ *   }

    38→ *
    39→ * Response:

    52→ * Features:
